rounds.text: The valuation of Rollatainers Ltd presents a significant disconnect between market pricing and fundamental health. While the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 8.41x [E1], this premium valuation is fundamentally undermined by a negative return on equity of -7.8%, which stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 10.27% [E8]. Investors are effectively paying a high multiple for a company that is currently failing to generate positive returns on shareholder capital [E1, E8]. Furthermore, the company offers no dividend yield, providing no income incentive to offset the risks associated with its negative profitability [E3, E8]. Conceded: [E5], [E7], [E10], [E36], [E37], [E38], [E47], [E54]. The reliance on high book value multiples in the absence of positive equity returns suggests that the current market price is not supported by the underlying financial performance of the business [E1, E8].

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 8.41x (price ₹ 3.11 on a book value of ₹ 0.37).
The stock sits 77% of the way up its 52-week range (1 low to 4 high).
P/E of 4.52x against a sector benchmark of 23.88x.
P/B of 8.03x against a sector benchmark of 2.51x.
ROA of 47.86% against a sector benchmark of 4.99%.
ROE of -7.8% against a sector benchmark of 10.27%.
EV/EBITDA of 5.36x against a sector benchmark of 14.14x.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 22 per share against a market price of Rs 3.11.
That leaves a margin of safety of 86.0%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies -13.3% earnings growth, against the 15.0% the base case assumes.
FUNDAMENTALS-LED — Profit grew 15% vs price 1% (5Y) — fundamentals outpacing the stock; potentially undervalued.
Screen reason (bull side): DCF margin of safety 86%
